request.system:
You read one Slack thread of a hardware engineering program.
The user message gives the channel purpose when it is known, the thread root and the changed messages.
The changed messages are the messages posted or edited since the thread was last read. This delta is the set of changed messages.
A thread root that is new in this delta is the first of the changed messages.
Give the probability, from 0 to 1, that the changed messages carry project information: a decision, a blocker, a risk, a schedule change, a spec change, a BOM change, an ask about the program, or an fyi that a program member needs to know.
Small talk, thanks and social messages are not project information.
Write the rationale first, then the probability.

messages.content:
Channel purpose: CAD, drawings, tolerances, tooling and mechanical FA

Thread root:
new in this delta: it is the first changed message below
Changed messages, oldest first:
[ts 1792167600.010071] author U0ME01: Top cover logo review is somehow still open. I’m saying the current font looks too soft once it’s embossed, and the depth feels like it will catch grime.
[ts 1792167780.010072] author U0EM01: I don’t care about the exact font as much as making sure it reads cleanly after texture. If the mark looks fuzzy on first articles, we’ll be annoyed forever.
[ts 1792168020.010073] author U0EE01: Please don’t make the emboss proud enough to become a wipe snag. The cover already gets handled a lot during service.
[ts 1792168260.010074] author U0ME01: That’s why I’m pushing shallower with a simpler face. The fancy font is doing us zero favors in molded plastic.
[ts 1792168500.010075] author U0FW01: From the FW side I have no stake in the font, but if this delays the top cover drawing release I’m voting for boring and readable.
[ts 1792168740.010076] author U0EM01: Let’s stop bikeshedding it here. <@U0ME01> pick the plainest option that meets tooling feedback and note the emboss as shallow in the drawing comments.

data.rationale: The changed messages are a new thread about a top cover logo emboss: font legibility after texture, emboss depth to avoid wipe snags, and a decision request. The last message is a direct decision/action: pick the plainest option meeting tooling feedback and note the emboss as shallow in drawing comments. This is a spec/drawing decision affecting top cover drawing release, so it carries project information within the CAD/drawings channel. Not purely social.
